html:
The Bosnian Church was a Christian church in medieval Bosnia, independent of both the Catholic and Orthodox hierarchies, active from the 1200s until the Ottoman conquest of 1463.

Its monks called themselves krstjani, Christians, and were led by a figure called the djed, or grandfather. Popes and Hungarian kings accused it of the dualist heresy of the Bogomils and sent crusades and Franciscan missionaries against it, but scholars still debate what it actually taught. Its clergy served as advisers and witnesses at the courts of Bosnian rulers. It had no strong institutions and faded quickly after the Ottoman conquest, which helps explain the wide conversion to Islam in Bosnia.
sum: The Bosnian Church was a Christian church in medieval Bosnia, independent of both the Catholic and Orthodox hierarchies, active from the 1200s until the Ottoman conquest of 1463.
